study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Jalbrzikowski et al., American Journal of Psychiatry, 2019
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Age-Associated Deviations of Amygdala Functional Connectivity in Youths With Psychosis Spectrum Disorders: Relevance to Psychotic Symptoms

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used AFNI's 3dLME program to compute linear mixed models for analyzing voxelwise developmental effects of amygdala connectivity. Subject was included as a random effect to account for non-independence of data from the longitudinal cohort. Linear, inverse, and quadratic forms of age were examined, with the inverse form providing the best fit for all significant clusters.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used the 3dLME program in AFNI to examine voxelwise developmental effects of age for each amygdala subregion in typically developing control youths. 3dLME is a group analysis program that computes linear mixed models (30). Subject was included as a random effect, which allows us to model and account for the non-independence of data (multiple visits) in the longitudinal cohort (31).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Jalbrzikowski2019.pdf.md: Methods / Statistical Analyses / Voxelwise developmental changes in amygdala subregion connectivity

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The response variable was resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) between amygdala subregions (centromedial and basolateral amygdala) and whole brain voxels. Specifically, voxelwise subject-level maps of Pearson correlations between the average amygdala subregion ROI time course and each voxel's time course were computed and Fisher r-to-z transformed.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We conducted voxelwise regressions on processed data using AFNI's 3dDeconvolve with the average of each amygdala subregion region of interest (centromedial, basolateral) time series as the seed... These analyses resulted in voxelwise subject-level maps of Pearson correlations (r) between the average amygdala subregion region of interest time course and each voxel's time course. R values were then normalized using the Fisher r-to-z transformation.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Jalbrzikowski2019.pdf.md: Methods / Statistical Analyses / Resting-state fMRI first-level statistical analyses

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Fixed effects included: age (linear, inverse, and quadratic forms examined), sex, and site. Subject was included as a random effect for longitudinal data. For sensitivity analyses, average framewise displacement was also included as a fixed effect covariate. The inverse form of age provided the best fit for developmental trajectories.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Age, sex, and site were included as fixed effects. Linear, inverse, and quadratic forms of age were examined... Subject was included as a random effect... To ensure that motion artifacts did not drive our results, we extracted the mean region of interest from the significant clusters and reran the linear mixed-effects models, including average framewise displacement as an additional fixed effect.
